findings.reason: without the base cold-roadmap arm the instrument is never shown able to detect a miss, so the node can close a measurement that measures nothing, and the plan should require the base cold-roadmap run first or state that a void control fails the node.
findings.text: §6's deliverable adds "If both arms cannot finish inside it, the run records the medians of every read that did finish and names each read that did not," and "A missed target attributed that way completes this node," but the done-when's only negative control is the base arm ("the base revision measured the same way in the same session, which must exceed the deadline for the comparison to count"); the escape clause is not conditioned on the control having run, so a run that exhausts the one-hour window completes the node with the base arm incomplete and no demonstrable control, and the two warm targets (warm roadmap ≤ 2 s, warm audit ≤ 3 s) — the ones the plan's own landed records show still missed (§16 close: warm roadmap 2.6 s) — are exactly the medians most likely to be dropped when the window runs out

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — the profiler `health-review-1010/health-tool-latency/scripts/profile_reads.py`, the §16 report `reads-remeasured-at-head/report.md`, the §9 profiles dir and the §1 table all exist; the §7 cross-references ("as §7 requires", "as §7 keeps its dumps") match §7's own text verbatim.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §6's escape clause lets the node complete with its declared negative control unrun.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the medians, every `.prof` dump and the pinned corpus revision are written to the run directory before the job ends, never left in the node-local scratch the corpus is extracted into.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §6 names no plan label, ticket or version tag; "§16 and §17" and "2026-10-16" are a section reference and a date the plan owns, not tracker identifiers.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — §6 states no root cause to contradict, its mechanism (the health review's profiler driving `mcp._roadmap`, `mcp._audit` and `discovery._discover_project` on a frozen corpus) can produce its medians on the real read path, and the node-acquisition mechanism ("naming the partition in the done-when") matches the dispatch contract that submits a separate `all_debug` job when the done-when names one.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §6 carries one deliverable, a measurement that decides whether the read fixes meet their targets; the conditional attribution and section proposal are the measurement's output, not a second goal.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §6 waits on §2–§5 and §8, §10–§14, §16, §17, every one of which is now `done` (declarations line 24), and both open followups (`f-araiid-remeasure` → §6, `f-araiid-018` → §18) point at the two implementable sections, so no open route dispatches at a completed unit.
